title: Custom render() with Provider
prompt:
When components depend on a context (theme, auth, query client...), every test would have to wrap them. Build a custom `renderWithTheme` that does it once.

**Requirements:**
1. In `test-utils.tsx`, import `render`, `RenderOptions` from `@testing-library/react`, and `ThemeProvider` from `./ThemeProvider`.
2. Export a function `renderWithTheme(ui: React.ReactElement, options?: RenderOptions)` that wraps `ui` in `<ThemeProvider value="dark">` and forwards all options to `render`.
3. In `Themed.test.tsx`, import `screen` from `@testing-library/react`, `renderWithTheme` from `./test-utils`, and `Themed` from `./Themed`.
4. Inside `it('renders with provided theme', () => { ... })`, call `renderWithTheme(<Themed />)` and assert `expect(screen.getByText('theme: dark')).toBeDefined()`.
hints: A custom render is just `(ui, options) => render(wrapper(ui), options)`. Re-exporting `screen` etc. from your utils file is also a common idiom.
Always forward `options` so callers can still use `container`, `wrapper`, `baseElement`, etc.
Tests under the wrapper consume context through their normal `useContext` calls -- no test-time API needed.
